title: Implement a Verbosity Level for Console Logging
description: The SynestheticML Forge is a sophisticated C-based machine learning framework. Currently, its logging output is static, which can be problematic for users who want either less clutter or more detailed debugging information during model training. This task involves introducing a configurable verbosity level to the system. The agent will need to modify the central configuration, update the command-line interface to control the setting, and finally, alter the logging implementation to respect the new configuration. This requires understanding how configuration, CLI parsing, and logging are interconnected within the framework.

project_spec.name: SynestheticML Forge
project_spec.description:
SynestheticML Forge (Project ID: c_ml_training_expert_015) is an expert-level C-based MLOps platform that trains, deploys, and continually refines multimodal generative models able to translate data from one creative domain into another (e.g., paint-stroke sequences → music chords, or perfume ingredient lists → color palettes).  

The system embraces Clean Architecture to keep its rich creative workflow—from dataset curation and feature engineering to model serving and automated retraining—loosely coupled yet highly cohesive. Each concentric layer (Entities, Use-Cases, Interface Adapters, Frameworks/Drivers) is implemented as a constellation of interchangeable strategies, pipelines, and observers, allowing artists, data-scientists, and engineers to remix components without breaking core business rules. 87 well-scoped files (≈599 k tokens) encapsulate features such as interactive data_visualization, hyperparameter_tuning via genetic algorithms, a model_registry with versioned creative artifacts, experiment_tracking with provenance graphs, and real-time model_monitoring that can trigger automated_retraining when a creative drift is detected—all while remaining faithful to C’s performance and portability.
dependencies: TensorFlow C API (low-level model graph manipulation)
Redis C client or SQLite (lightweight feature_store and experiment_tracking back-end)
